title: Verbs
description: Learn verbs for Grade 6: action, linking and helping verbs, transitive vs intransitive, regular vs irregular verbs, principal parts and subject-verb agreement — with practice and tests.

topics.title: Action, Linking & Helping Verbs
topics.concept:
Action verbs show what the subject does — physical (jump, write) or mental (think, believe).

Linking verbs do not show action; they link the subject to a word that describes or renames it. The common ones are forms of be (is, am, are, was, were) and seem, appear, become, feel, look, taste.

  • The soup is hot. (links soup → hot)
  • He became a doctor. (links he → doctor)

Helping (auxiliary) verbs work with a main verb to show tense, question or negative: be, have, do, will, shall, can, may — She does not play; will they come?

examples.problem: Action or linking? The flowers smell sweet.
examples.solution: Linking — here 'smell' links the flowers to the description 'sweet' (it isn't an action). Compare: 'She smells the flowers' (action).

examples.problem: Find the helping verb: We are watching a film.
examples.solution: are — it helps the main verb 'watching' show the present continuous.

recap: Action verbs show doing (physical or mental)
Linking verbs (be, seem, become, look) join subject to a description
Helping verbs (be, have, do, will, can) support the main verb

topics.title: Transitive & Intransitive Verbs
topics.concept:
A transitive verb needs an object to complete its meaning — it answers what? or whom?

  • She reads a book. (reads what? → a book)

An intransitive verb does not take an object; the meaning is complete on its own.

  • She sleeps. The baby cried.

Many verbs can be both: He sings (intransitive). He sings a song (transitive). Ask 'what?' after the verb — if there's an answer, it's transitive.

examples.problem: Transitive or intransitive? The dog barked loudly.
examples.solution: Intransitive — 'barked what?' has no answer; there is no object.

examples.problem: Find the object: Mother cooked delicious food.
examples.solution: Object = food (cooked what? → food). So 'cooked' is transitive here.

recap: Transitive verbs take an object (read a book)
Intransitive verbs need no object (she slept)
Test: ask 'what?' or 'whom?' after the verb

topics.title: Principal Parts & Subject–Verb Agreement
topics.concept:
Every verb has three principal parts: the base (V1), past simple (V2) and past participle (V3).

  • Regular verbs add -ed: walk – walked – walked.
  • Irregular verbs change form: go – went – gone; eat – ate – eaten; write – wrote – written.

Subject–verb agreement: a singular subject takes a singular verb; a plural subject takes a plural verb.

  • The dog barks. (singular → -s)
  • The dogs bark. (plural → no -s)

Note the twist: the verb adds -s for he/she/it, while the noun adds -s to become plural.

examples.solution: eat – ate – eaten (V1 – V2 – V3), an irregular verb.
play — 'boys' is plural, so the verb takes no -s.

recap: Principal parts: base (V1), past (V2), past participle (V3)
Regular verbs add -ed; irregular verbs change (go/went/gone)
Singular subject → singular verb (adds -s); plural subject → plural verb

Helping verb in 'I have done it':

Decide whether a verb is transitive or intransitive
Use the three principal parts of regular and irregular verbs

intro.en: A verb is a doing word or a being word — it tells what the subject does (run, eat, think) or what it is (is, seems, becomes). A sentence is not complete without a verb; it is the engine that makes the sentence move.
intro.hi: क्रिया (Verb) काम या अवस्था बताने वाला शब्द है — यह बताता है कि कर्ता क्या करता है (run, eat, think) या क्या है (is, seems, become)। बिना क्रिया के वाक्य पूरा नहीं होता; यह वाक्य का इंजन है।

real_life.situation:
Your coach shouts during practice:

Coach: Pass the ball! Run faster! You are doing well!
real_life.why: Pass and run are action verbs, are is a helping verb (with 'doing'), and in 'You are well' it would link the subject to a description. One short burst of speech shows all the verb types you'll learn here.

rule_box.formula: Action verbs DO · Linking verbs BE/BECOME · Helping verbs SUPPORT
rule_box.example: In "They have finished," 'have' helps and 'finished' is the main verb.

quick_test.explanation: Transitive verbs need an object to complete their meaning (read a book).

common_mistakes.note: Third-person singular adds -s/-es to the verb.
After 'has', use the past participle 'written', not 'wrote'.

fill_l1.instructions: Write the past tense (V2) of each verb.

sentence_correction.wrong: My friend go to college by bus.
sentence_correction.correct: My friend goes to college by bus.

reading.passage: Every morning, Arjun wakes early and runs in the park. He feels fresh afterwards. His sister Tara reads the newspaper while their mother cooks breakfast. By eight o'clock they have eaten, packed their bags, and left for school.

questions.q: Find one linking verb in the passage.
questions.answer: feels — it links 'He' to the description 'fresh'.

questions.q: Find one transitive verb with its object.
questions.answer: reads the newspaper (or cooks breakfast) — the verb takes an object.

questions.q: Identify a past participle (V3) used with a helping verb.
questions.answer: eaten (in 'have eaten') — the past participle of 'eat'.

speaking: She writes a letter every week.
He does not like loud music.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences about your daily routine, using one action, one linking and one helping verb.
writing.example: I wake up at six. I am brushing my teeth. The morning feels calm.

micro_quiz.q: Which is a linking verb in 'The cake smells good'?
micro_quiz.explanation: 'smells' links the cake to 'good' — no action here.

micro_quiz.q: The verb in 'She reads a novel' is:
Helping verb in 'They will come tomorrow':
micro_quiz.explanation: 'will' helps the main verb 'come' show the future.

challenge.q: Identify the verb type in 'The milk turned sour.'
challenge.explanation: 'turned' links the milk to the description 'sour' — linking.

challenge.q: Which sentence has a transitive verb?
challenge.explanation: 'painted a picture' has an object — transitive.
